symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Number of source-trial observations.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of target-population covariate observations.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Polynomial source-depletion exponent at the left boundary.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of each source conditional response.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the nonsingular source and target density factors.

symbols.name: \gamma
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Asymptotic target-to-source sample-size ratio.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: Common radius for boundedness and Hölder conditions.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: Known treatment-randomization positivity constant.

symbols.name: c_{S,-}
symbols.def: Lower bound for the nonsingular source density factor.

symbols.name: c_{S,+}
symbols.def: Upper bound for the nonsingular source density factor.

symbols.name: c_{T,-}
symbols.def: Lower bound for the target density.

symbols.name: c_{T,+}
symbols.def: Upper bound for the target density.

symbols.name: \mathcal X
symbols.def: One-dimensional baseline covariate support with a distinguished left boundary.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Baseline covariate in the population specified by context.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Randomized treatment in the source trial.

symbols.name: Y^S(d)
symbols.def: Source-trial potential outcome under treatment \(d\).

symbols.name: Y^T(d)
symbols.def: Target-population potential outcome under treatment \(d\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: Observed source outcome, equal to \(Y^S(A)\) under consistency.

symbols.name: O^S
symbols.def: Source observation \(O^S=(X,A,Y)\).

symbols.name: W^S
symbols.def: Full-data source unit \(W^S=(X,A,Y^S(0),Y^S(1))\).

symbols.name: X^T
symbols.def: Target-population covariate observation.

symbols.name: W^T
symbols.def: Full-data target unit \(W^T=(X^T,Y^T(0),Y^T(1))\).

symbols.name: F^S_{n,m}
symbols.def: Source full-data law at triangular-array index \((n,m)\).

symbols.name: F^T_{n,m}
symbols.def: Target full-data law at triangular-array index \((n,m)\).

symbols.name: \pi_S
symbols.def: Source observed-data projection \(\pi_S(x,d,y_0,y_1)=(x,d,y_d)\).

symbols.name: \pi_T
symbols.def: Target observed-data projection \(\pi_T(x,y_0,y_1)=x\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_{n,m}
symbols.def: Observed data \(\mathcal D_{n,m}=((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^m)\).

symbols.name: P_S
symbols.def: Observed source-trial law \(P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m}\) at index \((n,m)\).

symbols.name: P_T
symbols.def: Observed target law \(P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m}\) at index \((n,m)\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P_{n,m}
symbols.def: Triangular-array observed-data law \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\) of \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

symbols.name: f_S
symbols.def: Lebesgue density of the \(X\)-marginal of \(P_S\).

symbols.name: f_T
symbols.def: Lebesgue density of \(P_T\).

symbols.name: g_S
symbols.def: Nonsingular source factor \(g_S(x)=x^{-a}f_S(x)\) for \(x>0\), extended continuously to \(x=0\).

symbols.name: g_T
symbols.def: Nonsingular target factor \(g_T(x)=f_T(x)\).

symbols.name: e
symbols.def: Known trial randomization probability \(e(x)=P_S(A=1\mid X=x)\).

symbols.name: \mu_0
symbols.def: Source control response \(\mu_0(x)=\mathbb E_{P_S}[Y\mid A=0,X=x]\).

symbols.name: \mu_1
symbols.def: Source treated response \(\mu_1(x)=\mathbb E_{P_S}[Y\mid A=1,X=x]\).

symbols.name: \mu
symbols.def: Transportable conditional effect \(\mu(x)=\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\).

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: Identified observed-law integral \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx=\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu(X)]\); under the identification assumptions it equals the target average treatment effect.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Transport Riesz weight \(r(x)=f_T(x)/f_S(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Randomized-trial contrast \(Z=AY/e(X)-(1-A)Y/\{1-e(X)\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H^u(M)
symbols.def: The radius \(M\) Hölder ball of order \(u>0\) on \(\mathcal X\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Local-polynomial order \(p=\lceil s\rceil-1\).

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm{LP}}
symbols.def: Operator-norm constant for the order \(p\) boundary local-polynomial remainder on the unit Hölder ball.

symbols.name: \mathcal P_p
symbols.def: Set of real polynomials of degree at most \(p\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: A fixed nonzero \(C^\infty\) bump supported on \([0,1]\) with Hölder norm at most one.

symbols.name: \rho_n(a,s)
symbols.def: Source root-risk rate \(\rho_n(a,s)=n^{-1/2}\) for \(a<1\), \(\rho_n(a,s)=\sqrt{\log n/n}\) for \(a=1\), and \(\rho_n(a,s)=n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) for \(a>1\).

symbols.name: J_n
symbols.def: Deterministic calibration dimension \(J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Spline degree \(q=\lceil\max\{s,t\}\rceil\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_{h,J}
symbols.def: Degree \(q\) normalized B-spline space with endpoint-repeated equally spaced knots \(h+\ell(1-h)/J\), \(\ell=0,\ldots,J\), including the constant function.

symbols.name: c_{\mathrm{OT}}
symbols.def: Squared Euclidean transport cost \(c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)=|x-z|^2\).

symbols.name: \eta_0
symbols.def: Fixed entropic regularization level.

symbols.name: \lambda_0
symbols.def: Fixed source-marginal relaxation level.

symbols.name: \xi_n
symbols.def: Calibration-slack penalty \(\xi_n=n^2\).

symbols.name: K_0
symbols.def: Fixed number of cross-fitting folds, \(K_0=5\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Index of a deterministic source or target validation fold.

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: Index of a source observation.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: Index of a target observation.

symbols.name: \mathcal T^S_k
symbols.def: Source training complement \(\mathcal T^S_k=\{i:1+((i-1)\bmod K_0)\ne k\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal T^T_k
symbols.def: Target training complement \(\mathcal T^T_k=\{j:1+((j-1)\bmod K_0)\ne k\}\).

symbols.name: k_S
symbols.def: Deterministic assignment \(k_S(i)=1+((i-1)\bmod K_0)\).

symbols.name: k_T
symbols.def: Deterministic assignment \(k_T(j)=1+((j-1)\bmod K_0)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal V^S_k
symbols.def: Source validation fold \(\mathcal V^S_k=\{i:k_S(i)=k\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal V^T_k
symbols.def: Target validation fold \(\mathcal V^T_k=\{j:k_T(j)=k\}\).

symbols.name: N^S_k
symbols.def: Source validation-fold size \(N^S_k=|\mathcal V^S_k|\).

symbols.name: N^T_k
symbols.def: Target validation-fold size \(N^T_k=|\mathcal V^T_k|\).

symbols.name: \mathbf R_h
symbols.def: Scaled boundary basis \(\mathbf R_h(x)=(1,x/h,\ldots,(x/h)^p)^\top\).

symbols.name: \widehat G_{k,h}
symbols.def: Fold-trained ridge Gram matrix defined in \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\alpha_{k,h}
symbols.def: Unique fold-trained boundary ridge coefficient defined in \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\).

symbols.name: \widehat d_{k,h}
symbols.def: Deterministic derivative convention \(\widehat d_{k,h}(x)=\mathbf 1\{|\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}|<1\}\), with value zero at the two truncation kinks.

symbols.name: \mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)
symbols.def: The class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)
symbols.def: Worst-case root-mean-squared risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\).

symbols.name: b_h
symbols.def: Least-favorable boundary bump constructed from \(K\) at scale \(h\).

symbols.name: \widehat\mu_h
symbols.def: Order \(p\) boundary local-polynomial fit for \(\mu\) on \([0,h]\), spliced to an interior cross-fitted regression fit.

symbols.name: \mathbf b_{h,J}
symbols.def: Canonical left-to-right normalized B-spline basis of \(\mathcal B_{h,J}\), with its constant coordinate first.

symbols.name: \widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}
symbols.def: The vector obtained from \(\mathbf b_{h,J}\) by deleting its constant first coordinate.

symbols.name: \widehat P^S_h
symbols.def: For fold \(k\), the training-complement interior source measure \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h=|\mathcal T^S_k|^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\delta_{X_i}\); the fold superscript is suppressed when context fixes \(k\).

symbols.name: \widehat P^T_h
symbols.def: For fold \(k\), the training-complement interior target measure \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h=|\mathcal T^T_k|^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\delta_{X_j^T}\); the fold superscript is suppressed when context fixes \(k\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Pi_{h,J}
symbols.def: Unique calibrated semi-unbalanced entropic transport plan constructed in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\theta_{h,J}
symbols.def: The normalized nonconstant spline multiplier of the unique fold-trained transport program in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\psi_{h,J}
symbols.space: real vectors indexed by interior target training observations
symbols.def: The target-marginal multiplier of the fold-trained transport program, selected jointly with the calibration multiplier by the minimum-Euclidean-norm convention.

symbols.name: \widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT}}_{h,J}
symbols.def: Measurable dual-potential extension on all of \([h,1]\) constructed in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\); on training atoms it equals the first-marginal density of \(\widehat\Pi_{h,J}\).

symbols.name: \Delta_{h,J}
symbols.def: Cross-fitted interior calibration residual \(\Delta_{h,J}(v)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}
symbols.def: Boundary-spliced Riesz-calibrated transport estimator constructed in \(\mathrm{def:spliced\text{-}estimator}\).

symbols.name: \widehat U^T_{j,h,J}
symbols.def: Fold-held-out target plug-in summand defined in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\).

symbols.name: \widehat U^R_{i,h,J}
symbols.def: Fold-held-out weighted interior residual summand defined in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\).

symbols.name: \widehat U^B_{i,h,J}
symbols.def: Fold-aggregated boundary local-polynomial linear summand defined in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\).

symbols.name: \zeta_i^S
symbols.def: Independent standard-normal source multiplier, conditionally generated after observing \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

symbols.name: \zeta_j^T
symbols.def: Independent standard-normal target multiplier, conditionally generated after observing \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P^*
symbols.def: Conditional law, given \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), under which all \(\{\zeta_i^S:i=1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{\zeta_j^T:j=1,\ldots,m\}\) are mutually independent \(N(0,1)\) variables.

symbols.name: \mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}
symbols.def: Fold-centered source--target calibration-residual multiplier process constructed in \(\mathrm{def:calibration\text{-}residual\text{-}envelope}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}
symbols.def: Fold-centered multiplier analogue of the boundary local-polynomial linear term constructed in \(\mathrm{def:calibration\text{-}residual\text{-}envelope}\).

symbols.name: \widehat B_{h,J}
symbols.def: Fixed-class upper envelope for the absolute boundary smoothing and calibration bias of \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}\).

symbols.name: \widehat E_{h,J}
symbols.def: Conditional multiplier quantile envelope for the joint centered calibration-residual and boundary-linearization process at indices \((h,J)\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}
symbols.def: Cross-fitted standard-error estimate for the target empirical term, the interior calibrated residual term, and the boundary local-polynomial term.

symbols.name: \operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}
symbols.def: Folded-normal critical value \(\operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}(u)=\inf\{c:\inf_{|b|\le u}P(|N(b,1)|\le c)\ge1-\gamma/2\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{h,J}
symbols.def: Bias-aware interval constructed in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak G
symbols.def: A prespecified finite grid of candidate pairs \((a,s)\), including values on both sides of \(a=1\).

symbols.name: c_{\mathrm{ss}}
symbols.def: Lower persistence constant in the boundary self-similarity condition.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm{ss}}
symbols.def: Upper persistence constant in the boundary self-similarity condition.

symbols.name: h_0
symbols.def: Largest dyadic scale on which boundary self-similarity is imposed.

symbols.name: \mathcal M^{\mathrm{ss}}_{n,m}(a,s,t)
symbols.def: Boundary self-similar subclass constructed in \(\mathrm{def:self\text{-}similar\text{-}class}\).

assumptions.condition: \(e\) is fixed and known by the source-trial randomization protocol.
\(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

novel.justification: The condition permits polynomial depletion of trial enrollment at a clinically meaningful covariate boundary. Beta-type enrollment densities and smooth exponential tilts of \(x^a\) satisfy it, so it describes a concrete weak-overlap mechanism rather than an estimator-dependent rate restriction.

standard.name: target density bounded away from zero and infinity

assumptions.condition: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_S\)-almost every \(x\).
\(c_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\le\inf_{q\in\mathcal P_p}\sup_{x\in[h/2,h]}|\mu(x)-q(x)|\le C_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\) for every dyadic \(h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: The condition says that a leading boundary feature persists across resolution scales instead of disappearing through accidental polynomial cancellation. Functions of the form \(q(x)+cx^s+r(x)\), with \(c\ne0\), \(q\in\mathcal P_p\), and a smoother remainder \(r\), satisfy it, making the restriction interpretable and testable through adjacent-scale differences.

definitions.name: Polynomial-boundary transport class
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\bigl\{\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}:\exists(F^S_{n,m},F^T_{n,m})\text{ with }P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m},\ P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m},\text{ and every listed member-property assumption holds at the fixed indices }(n,m,a,s,t)\bigr\}.\] The finite-\((n,m)\) class contains no condition on how \(m/n\) behaves along a sequence.

definitions.name: Two-sample minimax root risk
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2},\] where the infimum ranges over all estimators measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

definitions.name: Executable cross-fitted boundary regression
definitions.construction: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set \[\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},\qquad \widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.\] Regress \(Z\) on \(\mathbf b_{h,J}\) using the same training indices with \(X\ge h\), the normalized least-squares objective, and ridge \(n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2\). Define \(\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(x)\) as \(\max\{-1,\min\{1,\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}\}\) for \(x<h\) and as the analogously truncated fitted spline for \(x\ge h\). Define \(\widehat d_{k,h}(x)=\mathbf 1\{|\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}|<1\}\), taking value zero at equality. Empty local samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridge, ordered basis, and stated kink convention make every fold fit and its boundary linearization unique.

definitions.name: Executable interior RiCOT weights
definitions.construction: For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy the nonredundant calibration equations \(\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\). If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of \[\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).\] Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus \(\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2\). Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the out-of-sample extension \[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.\] This formula is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J,1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\): it agrees with that density at every source training atom and is a positive measurable function at independent held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\).

definitions.name: Riesz-calibrated boundary-spliced estimator
definitions.construction: Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define \[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.\] Thus each displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), so the residual correction is not an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\).

definitions.name: Fixed-class bias envelope
definitions.construction: \[\widehat B_{h,J}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J}(v)|.\] The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\) from the two armwise radius-\(M\) balls, and the displayed support function is indexed by \(J\) through the fitted transport weight inside \(\Delta_{h,J}\).

definitions.name: Foldwise linear summands and standard error
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define the held-out target and interior-residual summands \[\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}=\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_j^T),\qquad \widehat U^R_{i,h,J}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.\] The source-side linear effect of estimating the boundary polynomial in every fold whose training set contains source observation \(i\) is \[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\widehat d_{k,h}(X_j^T)\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.\] Thus \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}\) is exactly the displayed first-order boundary local-polynomial training contribution to the target plug-in average, with the truncation derivative fixed by \(\widehat d_{k,h}\). For any fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define the fully observable standard error by \[\begin{aligned}\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J}).\end{aligned}\] The four lines are respectively the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and their within-source covariance. There is no primitive source--target covariance because \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\) is the product experiment; randomness of fold-trained coefficients is retained in every displayed summand and its asymptotic remainder is controlled in the honesty theorem. A term with fold size at most one is defined to be zero.

definitions.name: Multiplier calibration-residual envelope
definitions.construction: Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make \(\{\zeta_i^S:i=1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{\zeta_j^T:j=1,\ldots,m\}\) mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define the fold-centered calibration process \[\begin{aligned}\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].\end{aligned}\] Define the boundary contribution, using the exact local-polynomial linear summand from \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), by \[\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J}\right].\] The computable random envelope is \[\widehat E_{h,J}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.\] Empty-fold averages are zero; with the deterministic modulo allocation they are absent once \(n,m\ge K_0\). The same source multipliers appear in both source pieces, so their covariance is retained, while all target multipliers are independent of all source multipliers.

definitions.name: Bias-aware transported-mean interval
definitions.construction: Using only the statistics displayed in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), and \(\mathrm{def:calibration\text{-}residual\text{-}envelope}\), define \[\mathcal I_{h,J}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}\pm\operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}\!\left(\frac{\widehat B_{h,J}+\widehat E_{h,J}}{\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}}\right)\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}\right].\] If \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}=0\), define \(\mathcal I_{h,J}=\mathbb R\) when \(\widehat B_{h,J}+\widehat E_{h,J}>0\), and define the singleton \(\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}\}\) otherwise. No unreported fitted quantity or prose-specified variance component enters the interval.

definitions.name: Multiscale self-similar adaptation handle
definitions.construction: Use dyadic differences of adjacent boundary local-polynomial fits to estimate persistent boundary approximation error, estimate \(a\) from source empirical masses of dyadic boundary shells, and combine these diagnostics with interior Riesz-calibration residuals to select one pair from \(\{\mathcal I_{h,J}:h\text{ dyadic},\ J=\lceil h^{-1}\rceil\}\).

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) and \(h\downarrow0\), \[\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}^2=\int_h^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx\asymp\begin{cases}1,&a<1,\\ \log(1/h),&a=1,\\ h^{1-a},&a>1.\end{cases}\] Hence the target expectation functional has a source \(L^2(P_S)\) Riesz representer if and only if \(a<1\).
statements.justification: This norm is the precise regularity threshold behind the regular, critical, and nonregular regimes.
statements.gap: The transported control-regression component in Burman et al.'s distinct target-outcome estimand uses a density-ratio representer under bounded overlap, while Khan and Tamer link large inverse weights to irregularity without computing this polynomial-boundary threshold for the present covariate-only target functional.
statements.consumer: The lemma tells analysts of the RICOT cardiomyopathy transport study whether an ordinary influence-function variance is finite before fitting a transport estimator.

statements.statement: There are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for every sufficiently small \(h\), the perturbations generated by \(b_h\) yield two observed-data laws \(\mathbb P_{+,h},\mathbb P_{-,h}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) whose source marginals satisfy \[\operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,n},P_{-,h}^{S,n})\le Cnh^{2s+a+1},\qquad |\tau(\mathbb P_{+,h})-\tau(\mathbb P_{-,h})|\ge ch^{s+1}.\] A separate smooth target-density perturbation yields two full-data laws whose observed target projections have divergence bounded by a constant and target separation at least \(cm^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The witness converts the boundary geometry into the exact testing separation needed for the converse.
statements.gap: Zhang et al. define \(\mathcal V\) by the uniform bound \(\sup_x p^*(x)/p^\circ(x)\le B\) in Section 1 on page 2 and state its minimax lower bound as Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12; that construction does not cover a diverging polynomial boundary ratio, produce the exponent \((s+1)/(2s+a+1)\), or include the independent target-sample floor.
statements.consumer: The witness certifies that no alternative weighting method can improve the proposed cardiomyopathy transport rate merely by changing the optimizer.

statements.statement: For fixed \(a,s,t,M,\varepsilon,c_{S,-},c_{S,+},c_{T,-},c_{T,+}\) with \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), there is \(c>0\) such that \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] At \(a=1\), the source term is \(c\sqrt{\log n/n}\); it is obtained by a multiscale mixture of boundary bumps and has no hidden polynomial loss.
statements.justification: The converse is the theorem-level certificate that the three regimes are structural rather than artifacts of truncation.
statements.gap: Khan and Tamer establish tail-dependent irregularity. Zhang et al.'s uniformly bounded-ratio class is defined in Section 1 on page 2 and its known-law lower bound is Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12; neither result derives the two-sample polynomial-boundary phase diagram or its critical logarithm.
statements.consumer: The result gives trial planners a lower bound on how much source recruitment near an underrepresented cardiomyopathy-risk boundary is needed for a desired precision.

statements.statement: For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), the deterministic choices \(h=h_n\) and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\) give \[\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_n}-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2}\le C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] Uniformly over the same sequence, the fold-trained dual extensions evaluated on their held-out source folds obey \[\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}=O_P\!\left(1+\log(1/h_n)\mathbf 1\{a=1\}+h_n^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{a>1\}\right),\] \[\frac{\max_i\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2}{\sum_i\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2}=o_P(1),\qquad \sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h_n,J_n}(v)|=O_P\{\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls approximation of the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, whereas the product relation controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. These out-of-sample stability and residual bounds are conclusions derived from the primal program, its normalized dual extension, spline geometry, and primitive density conditions, not model assumptions.
statements.justification: This is the attainable procedure: interior calibrated transport preserves the RICOT geometry while boundary extrapolation regularizes the nonintegrable representer.
statements.gap: Burman et al.'s Proposition 2.1 on page 6 identifies their distinct target-outcome estimand and Theorem 3.1 on pages 6--7 gives its efficient influence function; under bounded population overlap in Assumption 1(iv) on page 7, Theorems 4.5 and 5.2 on pages 13--16 prove calibrated-weight consistency and efficient inference. Section S4.3 supplies the standard \(t>1/2\) threshold for one-dimensional density-ratio calibration-sieve approximation; this condition is distinct from the nuisance-product relation \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\). Their semi-unbalanced transport geometry informs this construction but is not a nested endpoint. Ma and Wang correct trimming bias for one-sample inverse weighting; neither result proves the displayed covariate-only transported-mean rate under a polynomial boundary ratio.
statements.consumer: The construction supplies a boundary-depletion sensitivity analysis for cardiomyopathy transport studies while preserving a calibrated optimal-transport geometry familiar from the RICOT application.

statements.statement: Under \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), in the special case \(a=0\), \(r(x)=g_T(x)/g_S(x)\) is uniformly bounded, \(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), and \[h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2},\qquad \int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx=O(1).\] The dual extension in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\) is strictly positive on every held-out \(x\in[h_n,1]\) whenever both training interior measures are nonzero, so the residual correction in \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_n}\) does not collapse to zero. Consequently its boundary bias, source stochastic term, and target empirical term are respectively \(O(n^{-1/2})\), \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and \(O_P(m^{-1/2})\), giving the ordinary two-sample root-risk reduction \(O(m^{-1/2}+n^{-1/2})\).
statements.justification: This calculation verifies that the repaired out-of-sample correction and the bandwidth arithmetic genuinely collapse to the regular root-rate case.
statements.gap: The statement is an internal sanity reduction for the present covariate-only target model, not a claimed specialization of Burman et al.'s different target-outcome estimand.
statements.consumer: Implementers can use this case as a unit test: fitted held-out correction terms must be nonzero and total root error must scale as \(m^{-1/2}+n^{-1/2}\).

statements.statement: For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), combining the preceding bounds gives \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\asymp m^{-1/2}+\begin{cases}n^{-1/2},&a<1,\\ \sqrt{\log n/n},&a=1,\\ n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)},&a>1.\end{cases}\] At \(a=0\), \(\mathrm{prop:a0\text{-}sanity\text{-}reduction}\) gives the bounded-ratio ordinary two-sample root rate directly for this covariate-only target model. Within the same model, \(0<a<1\) permits an unbounded but square-integrable Riesz weight without losing that root rate; \(a=1\) and \(a>1\) give its critical and nonregular continuations.
statements.justification: The theorem names the exact regular-to-nonregular frontier and supplies the required known-case reduction.
statements.gap: Khan and Tamer establish tail-dependent irregularity without this Hölder boundary modulus. Burman et al.'s Assumption 1(iv) on page 7 is a bounded-ratio condition for a different observed-target experiment and estimand, so it is an informed-by design anchor rather than a nested theorem comparator.
statements.consumer: The phase diagram turns boundary overlap diagnostics into an interpretable precision forecast for transporting a randomized cardiomyopathy effect to real-world patients.

statements.statement: For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\) obeys \[\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\}\ge1-\gamma,\] and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). Uniformly over the class, the explicit four-term statistic \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h_n,J_n}^2\) in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), including the covariance between \(\widehat U^R_{i,h_n,J_n}\) and \(\widehat U^B_{i,h_n,J_n}\), divided by the variance of the corresponding foldwise linear term converges in probability to one. The resulting studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of \(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_n}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_n}|\) approximates its centered sampling analogue with error \(o(1)\). The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, while the product relation controls the separate nuisance-product remainder. These approximations are derived from the product experiment \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\), bounded outcomes, the optimizer leverage bound in \(\mathrm{thm:ricot\text{-}attainment}\), and the entropy of the one-dimensional Hölder ball after spline-calibration projection. The conclusion includes \(a=1\), where the normal approximation is scaled by \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and the \(2M\) boundary-bias envelope remains explicit.
statements.justification: Point estimation alone is inadequate when regularization bias is of the same order as sampling uncertainty.
statements.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár give fixed-class local-polynomial intervals under regular designs, while Ma and Wang give tail-sensitive trimmed-IPW inference; neither covers a two-sample calibrated transport process with logarithmically diverging variance at \(a=1\).
statements.consumer: The interval supplies a prespecifiable, bias-aware uncertainty analysis for the RICOT cardiomyopathy application rather than a nominal Wald interval that can undercover under boundary depletion.

statements.statement: Fix \(a>1\), \(t>1/2\), and \(0<s_1<s_2\) such that \(s_\ell/(2s_\ell+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for \(\ell\in\{1,2\}\). Any confidence interval with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_1,t)\cup\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\) has, at some law in \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\), expected length at least \(c\{m^{-1/2}+n^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}\}\).
statements.justification: The theorem prevents data-driven smoothness selection from being advertised as honest without an explicit restriction that makes boundary bias observable.
statements.gap: Cai and Low characterize adaptation by between-class moduli, but the ordered modulus for a transported functional under source density \(x^a\), including the transition through \(a=1\), has not been computed.
statements.consumer: The result tells clinical transport analysts when prespecifying a smoothness class is unavoidable for valid interval length claims.

statements.statement: For fixed \(t>1/2\) such that \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for every \((a,s)\in\mathfrak G\), does the multiscale handle in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\) yield a single interval-valued procedure with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) uniformly over \(\bigcup_{(a,s)\in\mathfrak G}\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ss}}_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) and expected length of order \(m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\), up to the smallest unavoidable multiscale factor, at every member class?
statements.justification: This is the honest open content: boundary self-similarity may make both smoothness bias and the overlap exponent empirically detectable across scales.
statements.gap: Bull proves self-similarity results for adaptive function bands, and Armstrong and Kolesár treat bandwidth snooping, but neither establishes adaptation for a two-sample transported linear functional whose observation norm changes at \(a=1\).
statements.consumer: A positive answer would permit a defensible data-driven truncation analysis in RICOT applications while retaining honest coverage across plausible boundary-overlap regimes.

sampling_model.design: At each triangular-array index \((n,m)\), the observed law is \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\), induced by full-data laws \(F^S_{n,m}\) and \(F^T_{n,m}\) through the projections \(\pi_S\) and \(\pi_T\). The condition \(m/n\to\kappa\) applies only to theorem sequences.
sampling_model.units: Source full-data units are \(W^S=(X,A,Y^S(0),Y^S(1))\) and are observed as \(O^S=\pi_S(W^S)=(X,A,Y)\); target full-data units are \(W^T=(X^T,Y^T(0),Y^T(1))\) and are observed only as \(X^T=\pi_T(W^T)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary source treatment has known probability \(e(X)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The source density is \(f_S(x)=x^ag_S(x)\), where \(c_{S,-}\le g_S\le c_{S,+}\) and \(0<c_{S,-}\le a+1\le c_{S,+}\); the target density is \(f_T(x)=g_T(x)\), where \(c_{T,-}\le g_T\le c_{T,+}\) and \(0<c_{T,-}\le1\le c_{T,+}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Under the separate primitive conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, deterministic five-fold regression uses ridge-regularized order-\(p\) boundary local polynomials and degree-\(q\) interior B-splines. Interior weights solve the squared-distance semi-unbalanced entropic program with schedules \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), equally spaced knots, and \(J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\); normalized dual potentials give a measurable exponential extension evaluated on held-out source covariates. Inference uses the displayed fold-centered source and target multiplier process and the displayed target, interior-source, boundary-source, and source-covariance variance terms.

bibliography.citation: Burman, A., Gamalo, M., Ghosal, P., and Kundu, P. (2026). Transporting randomized trial effects to real-world populations via Riesz-calibrated optimal transport. arXiv:2608.23453v1. Their observed target unit includes \(Y^Q\). Proposition 2.1 on page 6 identifies \(\tau_Q=\mathbb E_Q[Y^Q]-\mathbb E_Q[\mu_0(X^Q)]\), while Theorem 3.1 on pages 6--7 gives the target and trial components of its efficient influence function. Bounded population overlap is Assumption 1(iv) on page 7; calibrated-weight consistency is Theorem 4.5 on pages 13--14; efficient inference for that estimand is Theorem 5.2 on page 16; Section S4.3 states the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration-sieve smoothness threshold \(t>1/2\); the cardiomyopathy application is Section 8 on pages 23--24.
Khan, S. and Tamer, E. (2010). Irregular identification, support conditions, and inverse weight estimation. Econometrica 78, 2021--2042.

Zhang, Z., Liu, X., Wang, S., and Teng, J. (2025). Minimax optimal two-stage algorithm for moment estimation under covariate shift. International Conference on Learning Representations. arXiv:2506.23453. The uniformly bounded likelihood-ratio class \(\mathcal V\) is defined in Section 1, page 2, and its minimax lower bound is Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1, page 12.
Donoho, D. L. (1994). Statistical estimation and optimal recovery. Annals of Statistics 22, 238--270.
Armstrong, T. B. and Kolesár, M. (2020). Simple and honest confidence intervals in nonparametric regression. Quantitative Economics 11, 1--39.
Armstrong, T. B. and Kolesár, M. (2018). A simple adjustment for bandwidth snooping. Review of Economic Studies 85, 732--765.
Ma, X. and Wang, J. (2020). Robust inference using inverse probability weighting. Journal of the American Statistical Association 115, 1851--1860.
Heiler, P. and Kazak, E. (2021). Valid inference for treatment effect parameters under irregular identification and many extreme propensity scores. Journal of Econometrics 222, 1083--1108.
Orihara, S., Komukai, S., and Li, F. (2026). Average treatment effect estimation via polynomial approximation and extrapolation under limited overlap. arXiv:2608.09329.
Cai, T. T. and Low, M. G. (2004). An adaptation theory for nonparametric confidence intervals. Annals of Statistics 32, 1805--1840.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For target data containing treated outcomes, Proposition 2.1 on page 6 identifies \(\tau_Q=\mathbb E_Q[Y^Q]-\mathbb E_Q[\mu_0(X^Q)]\), Theorem 3.1 on pages 6--7 gives its efficient influence function, and under bounded population overlap in Assumption 1(iv) on page 7, Theorems 4.5 and 5.2 on pages 13--16 give RICOT weight consistency and efficient inference for that distinct estimand.
Inverse-weighted parameters can be irregular and converge slower than the parametric rate when identification uses arbitrarily large weights.
The class \(\mathcal V\) in Section 1, page 2, imposes \(\sup_x p^*(x)/p^\circ(x)\le B\), and Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1, page 12, gives its moment-estimation minimax lower bound.
Folded-normal critical values deliver honest fixed-class local-polynomial confidence intervals with near-optimal expected length.
A bandwidth-indexed Gaussian-process critical value restores coverage after inspecting multiple bandwidths, including overlap-trimming applications.
Trimmed inverse-probability weighting can have Gaussian or non-Gaussian limits, and local-polynomial bias correction plus subsampling yields robust inference.
Between-class and ordered moduli determine lower bounds and constructions for adaptive confidence intervals on linear functionals.
Self-similarity is necessary and sufficient for honest adaptive confidence bands in the Hölder settings studied there.

tldr: A randomized trial may contain progressively fewer patients near a clinically important covariate boundary even when the real-world target population retains positive mass there. In the full-data triangular-array model, the causal target is identified as the observed-law integral \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\). The source contribution to root mean-squared error is \(n^{-1/2}\) below the square-integrability threshold \(a=1\), becomes \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) at the threshold, and is \(n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) above it, in addition to the independent target-sample term \(m^{-1/2}\). Under the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, a fully specified squared-distance Riesz-calibrated semi-unbalanced transport program is truncated to the overlap interior and spliced to a deterministic boundary local polynomial. Matching bump and multiscale lower bounds, a fully evaluable fixed-Hölder-class interval with a \(2M\) bias envelope and explicit foldwise multiplier and covariance terms, and a nonadaptation theorem complete the fixed-class program; honest joint adaptation is posed only on an explicit boundary self-similar subclass.

project_justification.gap: Regular Riesz-calibrated transport theory assumes enough overlap for a square-integrable representer, whereas irregular inverse-weight theory does not compute the sharp two-sample Hölder boundary frontier or its critical logarithm.
project_justification.niche: Polynomial trial depletion with a positive target boundary density creates an estimable causal mean whose information geometry changes exactly at \(a=1\); the target sample also imposes a separate parametric floor.
project_justification.fill: Under the separate primitive requirements \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, the project derives the matching modulus, derives optimizer stability for an executable calibrated-transport plus local-polynomial estimator, and provides fixed-class honest intervals with a fold-centered joint calibration--boundary multiplier envelope and an explicit covariance-complete standard error while making the self-similarity requirement for adaptation explicit.

related_work: Burman et al. (2026) are the optimization and application anchor, not a nested estimand comparator. Their target unit contains an observed outcome. Proposition 2.1 on page 6 identifies \(\tau_Q=\mathbb E_Q[Y^Q]-\mathbb E_Q[\mu_0(X^Q)]\), while Theorem 3.1 on pages 6--7 gives its efficient influence function; this core instead observes only target covariates and targets \(\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu_1(X)-\mu_0(X)]\). Their Assumption 1(iv) on page 7 imposes bounded target-to-trial density ratio, Theorem 4.5 on pages 13--14 proves calibrated-weight consistency, Theorem 5.2 on page 16 gives efficient inference for their estimand, and Section 8 on pages 23--24 studies 30-month mortality in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Section S4.3 is the source locator for the standard one-dimensional density-ratio calibration-sieve threshold \(t>1/2\). That threshold is separate from \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), which controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. The present transport program is informed by their semi-unbalanced entropic geometry without claiming that its \(a=0\) case reproduces their theorem. Khan and Tamer (2010) establish the general connection between arbitrarily large inverse weights and slower-than-parametric estimation, but do not analyze a two-sample transported Hölder functional. Zhang et al. (2025) define the uniformly bounded likelihood-ratio class \(\mathcal V\) in Section 1 on page 2 and state its minimax lower bound as Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12. Their observation model and Sobolev moment class differ, so their result informs the calibration and lower-bound comparison rather than being claimed as a theorem-level extension. Donoho (1994) supplies the modulus-of-continuity and affine-recovery blueprint used to turn the weighted boundary geometry into a minimax theorem. Ma and Wang (2020) show how local polynomial correction repairs trimming bias and how weak overlap changes limit laws; the present first proof step is instead a joint interior Riesz-calibration and target empirical process. Orihara, Komukai, and Li (2026) extrapolate a path of overlap-weighted estimands, but their key polynomial approximation condition is not the fixed-Hölder boundary remainder controlled here. Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) supply the fixed-class folded-normal critical value, while Armstrong and Kolesár (2018) explain the extra correction required after inspecting multiple scales. Cai and Low (2004) provide the ordered-modulus language for nonadaptation, and Bull (2012) supplies the multiscale self-similarity mechanism adapted in the open question.
technical_internal_limitation: The critical lower bound cannot follow from one boundary bump: a single bump at \(a=1\) yields only \(n^{-1/2}\). The \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) claim therefore stands or falls with a multiscale mixture whose likelihood divergence remains bounded while separations accumulate across scales. On the upper side, the convex-program stability, maximum-leverage control, spline calibration residual, boundary bias, target empirical noise, conditional multiplier approximation, and studentization must all be proved jointly from the primitive class. The primitive restrictions \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder are maintained separately; neither assumes a fitted-weight rate, optimizer stability, calibration rate, or normal approximation.
honest_scope: The fixed-class statements cover a one-dimensional boundary, known randomized-treatment propensity, bounded outcomes, the standard threshold \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, the separate product-smoothness relation \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, fixed transport penalties, and prespecified \((a,s,t,M)\). Each finite-\((n,m)\) minimax class is independent of the asymptotic balance condition; \(m/n\to\kappa\) is imposed only on theorem sequences. Within this covariate-only target model, \(a=0\) reduces to bounded-ratio regular two-sample transport and \(0<a<1\) permits unbounded but square-integrable weights at the same root rate. This reduction is not a specialization of Burman et al.'s target-outcome estimand. No unrestricted adaptive interval is claimed. Joint adaptation to \(a\) and \(s\) is confined to the explicit self-similar class and remains the first-class open-ended question. Multivariate boundary manifolds, observational treatment assignment, and formal sensitivity analysis for transportability are outside this core.
